novel_features.name: Idempotent send
novel_features.description: Skip the API call when a previous send with the same idempotency key already succeeded for this bot and chat — returns the original message_id instead of re-sending.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local store keyed on (bot_id, chat_id, idempotency_key); no Telegram CLI persists send identity, so cron retries always double-send.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever a cron job or agent retry might fire the same alert twice — it deduplicates without round-tripping the API.

novel_features.name: Replace-last status
novel_features.description: Edit the most recent message this bot sent to a chat in place — ideal for long-running job status that updates as steps complete.
novel_features.rationale: Reads the latest outbound row from the local messages table then calls editMessageText; falls back to send-new on 400. No competitor tracks 'last sent' per chat.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you would otherwise spam a chat with N status pings — one logical message that mutates over time.

novel_features.name: Sent-message history
novel_features.description: Browse the bot's outbound and inbound history filtered by chat, time window, sender, or media type — entirely from the local store, no API call.
novel_features.rationale: Every send and sync populates a local messages table; no Telegram CLI keeps any local history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an operator asks 'what did the bot say yesterday' — the answer is offline and audit-grade.

novel_features.name: Activity audit
novel_features.description: Roll-up of outbound activity — messages by chat, by media type, error rate, last-send timestamp — one shot, no API call.
novel_features.rationale: Pure SQL aggregation over the local messages table; the data exists nowhere else.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use as the weekly 'did the bot actually deliver' check or as the first step when diagnosing a delivery complaint.

novel_features.name: HTML preflight and safe-escape
novel_features.description: Validate or auto-escape HTML before sending — catches Telegram's 'can't parse entities' 400 before it leaves the box.
novel_features.rationale: Local lint against Telegram's allowed-tag whitelist with byte offsets, plus an escape pass for user-provided text. Competitors pass parse_mode through and fail only at the API.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for --html-escape when posting untrusted text, and `format html-lint` when debugging a 400 from a draft post.

novel_features.name: Channel publish with manifest
novel_features.description: Send a long-form post as one logical artifact — auto-split into chunks, recorded under a caller-chosen slug — then edit it later as a single unit.
novel_features.rationale: Tracks (slug → [message_ids]) so a later `publish edit` re-finds and re-edits only the changed chunks. No tool maintains this mapping.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for any multi-part broadcast that may be revised — release notes, status pages, weekly digests.

novel_features.name: Chat resolver
novel_features.description: Resolve an @username to a stable numeric chat_id with local caching — transparently falls back to the API when the cache misses.
novel_features.rationale: Local-store lookup; telegram-send uses a static config of named recipients, the opposite design — ours stays current when groups are upgraded to supergroups.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before send when you have a handle but need a numeric id (e.g., webhook payloads, persisted job state).

narrative.headline: Every Telegram Bot API method, plus idempotent sends, replace-last status messages, and a local store that knows what your bot said yesterday.
narrative.value_prop: telegram-pp-cli wraps the full Bot API (sendMessage, sendPhoto, edit/delete/forward, webhooks, chat admin, stickers) with the agent-native floor every Printing Press CLI gets — typed exit codes, --json, --dry-run, doctor — and adds a local SQLite store that powers send dedup, status-message threading, and audit roll-ups no other Telegram CLI offers. Designed for scripts and agents that need to send text and HTML messages to channels and DMs without re-implementing retry semantics every time.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in your environment. The token is appended directly into every API URL (`https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/<method>`); no OAuth, no refresh. `doctor` confirms the token by calling getMe and prints the bot identity so you can verify you're posting from the right bot before going live.

quickstart.comment: Verify TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is valid and print the bot identity. Run this once after setting the env var.
Send the smallest possible message to a channel. Exit 0 + JSON message_id confirms delivery.
Send a DM that is safe to retry from cron — same key, same outcome, no double-send.
Update the previous status message in place instead of sending a new one.
List everything this bot has said to this chat in the last day, read directly from the local store. Run 'telegram-pp-cli sync' first if you also want inbound messages.

troubleshoots.fix: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is unset or invalid. Run `telegram-pp-cli doctor` to confirm the token reaches getMe; re-create the bot via @BotFather if the token was revoked.

troubleshoots.symptom: Exit 4 with 'can't parse entities' on an HTML send
troubleshoots.fix: Run `telegram-pp-cli format html-lint --text "$BODY"` to find the offending offset, or re-send with `--html-escape` to auto-escape user-provided text.

Telegram allows 30 msg/sec globally and 1 msg/sec per chat. Throttle the caller, or replay failed sends from the local store using `messages list --since 1m  --json` (custom SQL via `sql 'SELECT \u2026'`) and re-send with backoff.

troubleshoots.symptom: send --replace-last returns 'message to edit not found' as a warning
troubleshoots.fix: Telegram does not allow editing messages older than 48 hours. The CLI automatically falls back to sendMessage in this case \u2014 the new message_id is in the JSON output.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for telegram-pp-cli when a script, cron job, or agent runtime needs to send Telegram messages reliably \u2014 especially when retries might fire twice (idempotency-key), when a status message should update in place (--replace-last), or when an operator needs to audit what was sent (messages list, audit). It is the right choice when you want a single Go binary that exposes the full Bot API plus a local store, instead of a Python interpreter dependency.
